'''Tatyana Polenova''' is a professor in chemistry and biochemistry at the [[University of Delaware]].<ref name=":0" /> She is the editor-in-chief of the ''[[Journal of Magnetic Resonance]]'' since 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tatyana Polenova, PhD|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/journal-of-magnetic-resonance/editorial-board/tatyana-polenova-phd|access-date=2021-05-27|website=www.journals.elsevier.com}}</ref> Her research interest involves using [[solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance]], combined with computational and other biophysical methods, to understand the structure, dynamics, and function of complex [[Macromolecular assembly|macromolecular assemblies]], both biological and inorganic.

==Education and career==
Polenova obtained her B.S. at the [[Lomonosov Moscow State University]] in 1992. She obtained her Ph.D. at [[Columbia University]] in 1997 and continued her postdoctoral research with [[Ann McDermott]]. She was appointed to assistant professor at [[Hunter College]] of the [[City University of New York]] in 1999, and moved to the University of Delaware in 2003, where she achieved full professor in 2011. She is the director of the [[NIH]]-[[Centers of Biomedical Research Excellence|COBRE]] "Molecular Design of Advanced Biomaterials" since 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|title=University of Delaware - Department of Chemistry & Biochemistry - Tatyana Polenova|url=https://www.chem.udel.edu/people/full-list-searchable/tpolenov?uid=tpolenov&Name=Tatyana%20Polenova|access-date=2021-05-27|website=www.chem.udel.edu|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Research==
Polenova uses [[nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy]] (NMR), specifically solid-state NMR, to investigate the structure and dynamics of biopolymers and inorganic materials.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Tatyana Polenova {{!}} University of Delaware|url=https://www.udel.edu/faculty-staff/experts/tatyana-polenova/|access-date=2021-05-27|website=www.udel.edu|language=en}}</ref> Her research focuses on the protein-based [[capsid]] assemblies of [[HIV-1]], the most common strain of the virus that causes [[HIV/AIDS]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=SelectScience|title=Professor Tatyana Polenova|url=https://www.thescientistschannel.com/tatyana-polenova|access-date=2021-05-27|website=www.thescientistschannel.com|language=en-GB|archive-date=2021-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627224051/https://www.thescientistschannel.com/tatyana-polenova|url-status=dead}}</ref> She has also investigated protein assemblies that are associated with [[microtubule]]s, important in the [[cytoskeleton]], where breakdown of these assemblies can lead to various diseases. To enable new insight on complex systems, she develops new solid-state NMR methods for fast [[magic angle spinning]] (40–110&nbsp;kHz), [[19F NMR]], and signal enhancement using [[dynamic nuclear polarization]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research {{!}} The Polenova Laboratory|url=https://sites.udel.edu/polenova-group/research/|access-date=2021-05-27|language=en-US}}</ref>
